page: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration features an ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache provisions include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) or network mounts for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps with zero included public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights distinct execution strengths across single-threaded and memory-intensive evaluations. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core execution with a score of 2361.0, alongside upper-tier rankings in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.29 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.08 GB/sec. PassMark memory testing also rates in the top tier at 3725.39. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench compilation, ray tracing, and Redis operations falls within median industry ranges. Cryptographic benchmarks exhibit reduced relative throughput, with PassMark CPU encryption ranking in the bottom quartile, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing reflects similar limitations.

The 2.0 GB per core resource footprint provides a compute-dense profile suited for tasks where raw single-thread velocity matters more than large working-set memory sizes. The lack of onboard NVMe storage represents an operational tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage architectures that consume baseline network allocations. Given the high single-thread scores and dedicated execution pipeline, c9g.2xlarge functions effectively for build and CI/CD pipelines, containerized web services, batch data manipulation, and lightweight inference deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, coupled with 16.0 GB of memory across a 2.0 GB per vCPU distribution. Local storage is not included, requiring external network block storage for persistence, while network bandwidth operates at a baseline of 4 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, particularly in Geekbench evaluation, PassMark memory bandwidth tests, and compression tasks such as gzip and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core compute performance and static web serving register in the median tier, whereas cryptographic acceleration shows weaker throughput. With its high clock speed and single-threaded execution efficiency, c9g.2xlarge fits CPU-bound tasks such as application compilation, microservice hosting, batch processing, and lightweight model inference.
